pr_title: Oculus requires apps with line when head tracking
pr_body:
Exporting the option in Godot's settings is unnecessary as in the option the head tracking feature is marked not required for use. 
Fixes #30854
pr_comments: @creikey The [Android documentation](https://developers.google.com/vr/develop/android/3dof-to-6dof) states that the tag **must** be omitted if the app doesn't support 6dof at all, so we should make it optional to not affect Godot regular android games.

With the latest WIP commit, it seems to be exporting correctly, and `apktool d` then inspecting the manifest file shows a correct file, however, upon uploading the APK  to a device, it complains about the binary being invalid without saying why. I'm looking into it right now. ( how do I tag this PR as a work in progress ? )
All of the bugs seem to be worked out now
@akien-mga The PR is ready for merging (once the commits are squashed), unless you have additional feedback.
I've squashed the commits in the latest force push.

issue_context.title: Exported oculus quest games treated as go games
issue_context.body:

**Godot version:**

e4ec59b6ae7ba4da8a57d35a4763192fd84fa358

**OS/device including version:**
<!-- Specify GPU model and drivers if graphics-related. -->
 Arch Linux

**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
Exported android game is missing extra android feature line in the manifest needed for the oculus quest to give the game 6dof tracking on the controllers: https://www.reddit.com/r/OculusQuest/comments/chjpu5/fix_for_sideloadedhomebrew_apps_and_games_with/

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Follow steps on the [oculus mobile github](https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_oculus_mobile) to export for oculus quest
2. Modify the demo to include controllers with a simple meshinstance as children for visualization
3. Controller tracking does not work due to the missing line in the manifest. 

**Minimal reproduction project:**
<!-- Recommended as it greatly speeds up debugging. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
comments:
After adding the line `<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.vr.headtracking" android:required="true" android:version="1"/>` as discussed in the reddit thread to the manifest the issue still "manifests". I've attatched the modified demo project with controller tracking so the issue can be reproduced. 
[demo.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3438041/demo.zip)
@m4gr3d yes, the controller tracking was working correctly. I'll look into it as well and let you know if I find anything.

It turns out that the controller tracking will work correctly if the line is added to the manifest, I was testing with a modified version of the godot oculus mobile plugin that had a bug in it. Apologies.

No problems, and thanks for the update!
Are you still working on a PR for the manifest fix, or should I handle it?

@m4gr3d I've created a pr for it at #30902  that just adds the line to the manifest with android required being false. If it's required to have it be an optional setting by the godot devs, then I can sort through the strange binary android manifest parser in the android platform's `export.cpp`

review_comments: This should also check if 'Oculus Mobile VR' is selected as Xr mode, since that tag is only valid for Oculus devices at the moment.

Rather than silently not adding the tag if it's not an oculus mobile device, I was hoping that in the godot_oculus_mobile docs it'd just specify to have the dropdown selected to the 6dof option if targeting the oculus quest.

One of the most important UX learning is that typical users never read the documentation, and so, if a feature has the potential to have a negative impact, then that feature should be placed behind a check to ensure that the feature is not accidentally enabled by the user.

This applies here as well since based on the [Google docs](https://developers.google.com/vr/develop/android/3dof-to-6dof) the tag **must** not be included for apps with no 6DoF features.

As you mentioned, we'll include a description of the dropdown's purpose in the docs, but a check is also needed in case the user doesn't read the doc or forget about it.
I've added a check then a warning print if the user forgets to set the xr mode.
Can the logic be extended similar to what's done with the permissions, so that we can have a list of `uses-features` tag that would be iterated through and added as specified by the user.
I'm not exactly sure how this could be done as the 6dof option and the 3dof plus 6dof option are mutually exclusive.

I was referring to other features besides 3dof/6dof that also necessitate the insertion of the `uses-features` tag.
For example, the [ARCore PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/26221/files#diff-b39419f9be37c6f37a62e693300244d1R19) needs to include the `android.hardware.camera.ar` `uses-features` tag.

Feel free to punt on this though since it won't be needed until that PR is ready to be reviewed, at which time, we can expand on the current insertion logic.
I'm working on this feature now.

Given that to add a general purpose features list would require changing some engine code that I cannot find currently where the Tree is constructed with checkboxes for features to allow setting android version and GL version etc, and the manifest line for the oculus quest is highly customized, this should be punted until that is done in a separate PR. As of right now, oculus quest support along with non 6dof oculus devices like the oculus go is completely broken without this modification, so it should be merged now.

Sounds good to me. Once you squashed the commits, it should be good to go.
Great work by the way!
